options.name: resolver.feature-unification = "workspace"
options.status: Not usable on the pinned toolchain. Verified: cargo 1.97.1 prints `warning: ignoring resolver.feature-unification without -Zfeature-unification`; -Z is refused on stable. Tracking issue open; partial stabilization of workspace mode proposed 2026-09-17; blockers listed 2026-07-22 include cargo tree output (#16583), --workspace --exclude behaviour, tests and the option's name. No release found that stabilizes it.
options.expected_gain_here: At most the dependency-identity duplicates: 1 of 4 linked viewer_timeline copies, plus part of 0.75 GiB of rlib copies per target. Measured via cargo tree: -p harness-view resolves 19 of 62 packages differently from --workspace (8 members, plus sha2, digest, syn, smallvec, zerocopy and others), so lane -p runs would stop differing from the round default unit.
options.selection_and_round_effect: -p still builds only the selected packages, but with workspace-wide features: -p harness-view changes from ['default'] to ['asset-local-test-host','default']. Round feature units keep their --features differences, so they still multiply, and they would stop testing a crate under only its own unification. The round default unit gains nothing: F-R47-8 already builds --workspace, the stable equivalent.
options.proof_or_isolation_risk: Changes what a -p lane proves. Forces a full round (CX-VAL-011). Field report: target-blind unification can enable native-only features (2026-09-26 comment).
options.probe: None until it reaches stable. Recheck #14774 at each toolchain bump; then `cargo tree -f '{p}|{f}'` with and without the setting, no build needed.
options.verdict: REJECTED now; recheck at toolchain bump.

questions.answer: A PDB is always written on MSVC. debug = 0 should cut this PDB by about two thirds; strip and split-debuginfo do nothing useful.

options.name: debug = 0 (builder lanes)
options.facts: rustc 1.97.1 MsvcLinker::debuginfo takes `_strip`, never reads it, and always passes /DEBUG. Local proof: build scripts (cargo debug=false when possible) have .pdb files, median 1.5 MiB for a 0.25 MiB exe, and the clap-gain fixture built with debug=0 and strip=symbols has a 1.25 MiB PDB.
options.expected_gain_here: ESTIMATE from streams: S_PUB32, DBI, public hash and std stay, about 85 to 90 MiB of 278, so PDB about -68 percent. Exe unchanged, so exe + pdb about -53 percent: a 47 GiB target to about 22 GiB. Link time should fall with the PDB; no number here. perf-book: dropping from full debug saves 20 to 40 percent and line-tables-only keeps most of that, so compile time gains little.
options.backtraces_and_reports: Lost: file and line in frames, and names of local procedures (18233 S_LPROCREF here) may resolve to a wrong neighbouring symbol (UNVERIFIED). Kept: `panicked at file:line:col`, expected from compiled-in Location data (confirm in the probe), plus assert messages and junit output. Today's reports contain no frames at all, so they lose nothing measured. What a lane loses is on-demand RUST_BACKTRACE=1 and native-crash analysis; it can rebuild that one case at line-tables-only.
options.proof_or_isolation_risk: Lane-only knob in studio-env.sh: no round proof changes. Profile is in unit_id, so each reused target rebuilds once. run-round overrides the two profile env vars itself, so it cannot leak into rounds.
options.verdict: ADOPT in lanes if the probe keeps panic locations.

options.name: debug = 0 for third-party only ([profile.dev.package."*"])
options.expected_gain_here: ESTIMATE PDB about -25 percent (48.4 MiB modules plus their share of procedure refs). toptopduck saw about -30 percent going from full debug to line-tables-only on dependencies, at very similar binary sizes (EXE 70 to 95 MB, PDB 414 to 482 MB after).
options.proof_or_isolation_risk: Requires root Cargo.toml, so a checked-in change that forces a full round. Keeps workspace line numbers, so it is the fallback if rounds refuse debug = 0.

options.name: line-tables-only (current)
options.facts: Keep for rounds until a decision. Types are already 2 percent of the PDB, so there is nothing more to gain at this level.

options.name: split-debuginfo
options.facts: On Windows MSVC only packed is supported, and it is already the default. off and unpacked need nightly -Z unstable-options.

options.name: strip
options.facts: Unread by the MSVC linker path. The docs note that before 1.79 strip unintentionally disabled PDB generation; that is gone.

options.name: -Clink-arg=/DEBUG:NONE (no PDB at all)
options.expected_gain_here: ESTIMATE exe + pdb -76 percent (364 to 86 MiB). Whether a later /DEBUG:NONE overrides rustc's /DEBUG is UNVERIFIED.
options.backtraces_and_reports: Frames lose names as well as lines. Panic locations should stay.
options.proof_or_isolation_risk: RUSTFLAGS enters unit_id and invalidates everything; no native-crash analysis.
options.probe: Optional extra variant only if V2 is not enough.

questions.answer: The workspace uses link.exe. rust-lld is present in the pinned toolchain, used in real Windows configs, and likely faster for these binaries; the size of the gain varies widely and must be measured.

options.name: rust-lld via linker setting
field_numbers: toptopduck, closest match (merged 2026-11-02): per-binary link about 16 s to about 2 s; batched cargo test --no-run 240.3 s to 121.9 s (-49 percent). Mixed with a dependency debuginfo cut, so not linker alone.
rust#71520 comment 2026-11-06, ripgrep, rustc 1.96, Dev Drive: run_linker 1020 ms to 712 ms (-30 percent); hello.rs 13 ms slower.
spookery (closed 2026-10-17, small project): test compile 64 s to 48 s, about 7 s saved overall at equal cache state; not worth it there.
Bevy enables rust-lld by default for Windows in its fast-builds config. perf-book: not default on Windows yet, should work for most use cases.
options.expected_gain_here: ESTIMATE 25 to 85 percent of link time, large only if linking dominates as R57 suggests. PDB size effect UNVERIFIED. Applied to the harness pair units (7635 s in R57): perhaps 3800 to 5700 s after.
failure_modes: #71520 still open, not default. Listed blockers (TLS alignment #72145, thin-LTO access violations #81408 and #111480, libtest undefined symbols #68647, manifestdependency .drectve #85642) were reported resolved in Dec 2024 except that bjorn3 notes platform-specific bugs will remain. Check #85642 for any binary that needs a manifest.
One-time rebuild of everything in a target when the setting changes (spookery +4 min, toptopduck 212 s). Costs one rebuild on each reused target.

Native objects: rav1e nasm output and rquickjs-sys C objects are linked in some feature units. Link them in the probe only if the probe crate reaches them; otherwise step 4's canary and full round are the proof. No /GL use is known, UNVERIFIED.

Parallelism: lld defaults to all hardware threads (verified in /? of 22.1.6). With jobs = 8 on the shared host that can oversubscribe; the 2026-10-24 OS error 1455 is a memory warning. Mitigate with -Clink-arg=/threads:4 only if the probe shows pressure.

Fixtures: run-round's clap-gain build inherits a checked-in linker setting. lld supports /Brepro (verified) but the library sha256 changes once; the corpus path is content-addressed. A lane `run-round --dev` that inherits a lane-only linker env could write a different sha and race a real round (exit 76).

Env leak: run-round does not clear CARGO_TARGET_*_LINKER. A round started from a shell that sourced studio-env.sh would use it, breaking CX-VAL-007. Have run-round unset or refuse it in step 0 before any lane adopts the knob.
options.proof_or_isolation_risk: Lane-only: none for proof, with the env-leak guard. Rounds: a checked-in .cargo/config.toml change, full round required (CX-VAL-007, CX-VAL-011). Rounds would test binaries linked differently from link.exe; host product linking is decided separately.
options.probe: Step 1 variant V1. Link phases can be read with lld /time.
options.verdict: ADOPT in lanes if the probe passes; rounds in step 4.

options.name: System lld-link from Program Files/LLVM
options.facts: Present at 22.1.0, but outside rust-toolchain.toml, so machine-local and unpinned.

questions.answer: Biggest single gain, and most of it comes from two crates. nextest keeps one process per test, so the usual shared-process risk does not apply.
questions.field_numbers: Cargo's own test suite: compile 3x faster, artifacts 5x smaller. corrode cites up to 50 percent. playwright-rs reports 53 binaries to 1 with nextest. No Windows measurement found.

counts.all_crates: 768 targets to about 72: one per crate plus keep-outs (16 files with global_allocator in 11 crates, 13 [[test]] entries in 6 crates with required-features or special needs). Per-round estimate at R57: about 2752 links to about 180.
counts.harness_pair_only: 105 targets to 3 (harness-view keeps 1 global_allocator file out). R57 and R58 links in the pair: 1524 to 24.
counts.space_estimate: One merged pair is about 0.37 to 0.45 GiB per own feature set, from the measured closure size plus own module streams. retime-output 46.1 to about 2.3 GiB; entry-references 41.8 to about 1.8 GiB; type-authored 60.6 to about 3.2 GiB; about -95 percent of those bytes. Full-round disk not measured: C: studio-round was left alone during R59.
counts.time_estimate: ESTIMATE: R57 pair units 7635 s to 1100 to 2500 s, saving 5000 to 6500 s of 13699 s wall (about 40 percent). Default unit also falls if all crates merge. Depends on link dominance: the probe measures it.

risks: Test identity: nextest binary ids and names change (hsk-studio-x::foo foo_test becomes hsk-studio-x::all foo::foo_test). 797 `--test NAME` occurrences in 206 files of the Studio records, and proof commands in live briefs, stop working or need `-E`. run-round derives filters from the list, so its code holds; verify comparisons across rounds and CX-VAL-002 reuse naming. Mitigate by recording an old-to-new map and checking equal test counts per unit.
Edit cost with incremental off: one test edit recompiles all modules of that merged crate instead of one file. Measured by V4. Mitigate by splitting by feature group if it hurts.

File-level cfg: 71 of 73 harness and 32 of 32 harness-view files use #![cfg(...)]. Inner cfg works on a module file, so per-feature behaviour stays; the merged binary simply shrinks per set. No longer-gated files need a check.

Blocking cases: global_allocator (16 files), any file with its own harness or crate-level attributes (62 files across crates with other inner attributes, 6 in the pair), shared helpers declared by `mod` in many files (53 and 28 in the pair) or #[path] (12), include paths relative to the file (15 in the pair), current_exe (4 in harness). `fn main` appears in viewer_timeline_nest_2; check whether it is a real entry point.
A compile error in one test file now blocks that crate's whole test binary; every test in that crate fails to build instead of one target.
Process isolation holds under nextest; doctests and any libtest use of the merged binary would share a process, and the workspace refuses plain cargo test already.

Round feature units: -p CRATE --features SET stays; round-features.toml only needs its comments naming test files updated. .config/machine-paths.toml pins counts per test file path, so keep files in place (autotests = false plus #[path] mod lines) or update it through the steward; a move would otherwise trip that policy check (exact step not traced).
questions.proof_or_isolation_risk: Product test layout change, in the crates' own MTs. Not a toolchain, lockfile or entrypoint change, so not forced full by CX-VAL-011 on that ground, but those crates' closure is re-selected and a lead may want one full round for the identity change.
questions.verdict: ADOPT for harness-view and harness after the probe; other crates only where a target shows it matters.

probe_step_1.crate: hsk-studio-harness-view with --features viewer (R58 unit: 312 s, 136 tests, 32 targets). Chosen because it holds the largest copies and has a round baseline.
probe_step_1.isolation: A throwaway tree at the candidate SHA and one STUDIO_OWNER per variant (cargo-probe-v0 to v4), each its own target. Same disk for all variants, one at a time under the normal lock. Never push; never run during a round on the same disk. Delete only under normal approval.
probe_step_1.commands: source studio-env.sh after setting STUDIO_OWNER, then for each variant export its setting AFTER sourcing. Run A: cargo nextest run -p hsk-studio-harness-view --features viewer --no-run --timings. Run B: touch crates/hsk-studio-harness-view/src/lib.rs, repeat. Run C: touch one tests file, repeat. Then cargo nextest run with the same selection.

variants.setting: best of V0 to V3, plus one merged target: autotests = false, [[test]] name = all, tests/all.rs with #[path] mod lines, keep-outs listed. Probe tree only.

probe_step_1.record_for_each: Seconds of A, B, C from the Finished line; GiB of exe and pdb in debug/deps; size of one viewer test exe and PDB; test count and pass count; cargo-timing.html path; any linker warning; whether the host showed OS error 1455.
probe_step_1.failure_report_check: In the throwaway tree only, one uncommitted tests/zz_probe_panic.rs that panics in a helper. Run it with and without RUST_BACKTRACE=1 in V0, V1, V2. Compare the `panicked at` line and the frames.

adoption_gates.V1: Run B at least 20 percent faster than V0, same tests pass, no new linker warning that matters, backtrace still symbolized at line-tables-only.
adoption_gates.V2: PDB at least 40 percent smaller, `panicked at` location unchanged.
adoption_gates.V4: exe + pdb at least 80 percent smaller, same test count and same names modulo the module prefix, Run B faster, Run C not more than Run B of V0.

probe_step_1.cost: Each variant compiles the closure once (about 60 packages) and relinks 32 binaries twice. UNVERIFIED total; plan for a few hours of one disk slot. V4 needs a small test-layout edit in the probe tree.

ranked_recommendation.step: Run the probe above on hsk-studio-harness-view.
ranked_recommendation.expected_gain: Replaces the estimates below with measured numbers. No lasting change.

ranked_recommendation.step: If the gates pass: lane-only rust-lld and debug = 0 in studio-env.sh, with STUDIO_DEBUG to opt back to line-tables-only for a failure, and run-round step 0 unsetting or refusing CARGO_TARGET_*_LINKER. Apply to new targets, or to reused ones at their next natural invalidation, since each reused target rebuilds once.
ranked_recommendation.expected_gain: ESTIMATE link time -25 to -85 percent; test bytes about -50 percent in lanes. Round proof unchanged.

ranked_recommendation.step: Merge integration tests of hsk-studio-harness-view and hsk-studio-harness into one binary each, with an old-to-new test name map; update briefs that use --test.
ranked_recommendation.expected_gain: ESTIMATE 105 targets to 3; about -95 percent of those crates' test bytes (46 GiB to about 2 GiB in a large lane); R57 pair links 1524 to 24, about 5000 to 6500 s off a 13699 s round.
